unit.title: An enum that guards its own transitions
Bug hunt: an enum that guards its own transitions

fund-java/04-classes-records-and-enums/0.instructions:
**Skills:** enums with behaviour · EnumSet  
**Level:** ★★☆

**Interview prompt.** "Support agents keep moving shipped orders back to draft. Put the allowed status transitions in the type itself."

**Why it matters.** Enums are classes: a constant can carry data and behaviour, so the state machine lives in one place instead of in every service method.

**Your task.** Complete the nested `enum Status { DRAFT, PLACED, PAID, SHIPPED, CANCELLED }`:
- `boolean canMoveTo(Status target)`: DRAFT → PLACED; PLACED → PAID; PAID → SHIPPED; any of DRAFT, PLACED or PAID → CANCELLED; nothing else (in particular no transition out of SHIPPED or CANCELLED, and no "transition" to the same status)
- `Status moveTo(Status target)` returns `target` when allowed and throws `IllegalStateException` otherwise
- `static Status parse(String code)` accepts a status name in any letter case with surrounding whitespace ("  paid " → PAID) and throws `IllegalArgumentException` for anything else (including null)

**Worked example.** `Status.PAID.canMoveTo(Status.SHIPPED)` is true; `Status.SHIPPED.moveTo(Status.DRAFT)` throws.
hints: The rules depend on the current constant, so the method can switch on this.
Let the current constant decide its legal targets in one switch, refuse an illegal move with an exception, and parse by tidying the text before looking the constant up, rejecting a missing value.

Let each status answer which targets are legal from where it stands, refuse illegal moves with an exception, and for parsing tidy the text and match the constant name case-insensitively, rejecting a missing value.

fund-java/04-classes-records-and-enums/0.instructions:
**Skills:** debugging · enums with behaviour · EnumSet  
**Level:** ★★☆

**Bug hunt.** The code in the editor is a plausible first attempt at drill 1, "An enum that guards its own transitions". It passes some of the tests, but it has one real bug, the kind a reviewer should catch before it ships.

**Your task.** Find the bug and fix it, changing as little as you can; the tests are the same as drill 1's. The spec is unchanged: Complete the nested `enum Status { DRAFT, PLACED, PAID, SHIPPED, CANCELLED }`:
- `boolean canMoveTo(Status target)`: DRAFT → PLACED; PLACED → PAID; PAID → SHIPPED; any of DRAFT, PLACED or PAID → CANCELLED; nothing else (in particular no transition out of SHIPPED or CANCELLED, and no "transition" to the same status)
- `Status moveTo(Status target)` returns `target` when allowed and throws `IllegalStateException` otherwise
- `static Status parse(String code)` accepts a status name in any letter case with surrounding whitespace ("  paid " → PAID) and throws `IllegalArgumentException` for anything else (including null)
fund-java/04-classes-records-and-enums/0.explanation:
The planted bug is in `parse`: it upper-cases but does not strip, so `"  paid "` becomes `"  PAID "`, and `valueOf` accepts only the exact constant name. "parse ignores case and whitespace" fails with "No enum constant ... PAID"; every transition test passes, because the rules were already right. The fix adds one call:

```java
return Status.valueOf(code.strip().toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT));
```

`trim()` instead of `strip()` also passes these tests, which only use ASCII spaces; `strip()` additionally removes Unicode whitespace. Keep `Locale.ROOT` on the upper-casing, so a server running in a Turkish locale still turns `"paid"` into `PAID`.
hints: Parse " paid " with the spaces a form might send.
valueOf matches the exact constant name, and the surrounding spaces are part of the string.
Remove surrounding whitespace before upper-casing and looking the name up.
